A1.justification: Both are readable 11-page versions of the same UNITE paper, with matching scientific text, equations, four tables, and six figures. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary material.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.4 report original UNITE detection results, three-class evaluations, attention visualizations, and ablations in Tables 1-4 and Figures 3-6.

after.justification: The same original empirical results remain in Tables 1-4 and Figures 3-6, including cross-dataset detection and ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same frozen SigLIP features, four-block transformer with 12 attention heads, positional encoding, and combined cross-entropy and attention-diversity loss. No procedure or component changes.

E1.justification: Both use the same face-manipulation datasets, AVID background videos, GTA-V, DeMamba, and NYTimes videos. Binary detection, three-class classification, and T2V/I2V generator coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2 and 3, including TALL and PUDD in the face-manipulation comparison and the same F3Net, NPR, STIL, and CLIP/DeMamba variants in the synthetic-video comparison.

E3.justification: The FF++/GTA-V training configurations, DeMamba validation split, evaluation metrics, binary and three-class protocols, and training budgets are unchanged. Both retain the same frame-count and transformer-depth evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the attention-heatmap examples, CE/AD loss ablations with and without GTA-V training data, and frame-count and transformer-depth analyses in Figures 3-6. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 retain identical numerical entries, and Figures 3-6 retain the same findings. For example, Table 3 reports UNITE average precision of 92.76% and recall of 89.60% in both versions.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, assumptions, positional encoding, feature-center updates, and loss equations (1)-(6) are unchanged. No formal result, derivation, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about full-frame synthetic-video detection, attention diversity, synthetic training data, and cross-domain performance.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting attention diversity and GTA-V training to generalization remain unchanged, as does the interpretation that greater transformer depth overfits. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same sampling and padding procedures, feature dimensions, loss hyperparameters, AdamW schedule, TensorFlow implementation, and eight-TPUv3 training hardware. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the same 64 references retain identical research positioning. The changed page back-reference for reference [6] and the new publication-status footnote do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds a title-linked footnote stating publication at CVPR 2025 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, section order, and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The footnote causes text reflow. On page 8, Figure 5 moves from the left column to above Figure 6 in the right column, and the conclusion extends onto page 9. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds publication metadata and adjusts layout while retaining the same methods, evidence, claims, and reproducibility information. These changes establish no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
